risks.risk_description: Cybersecurity is a ubiquitous concern with organizations facing high or very high risk of cyber attacks and breaches, impacting data security and operational continuity.

risk_driver.driver_description: Increasing reliance on digital systems and IT infrastructure exposes organizations to cyber threats.
Cyber attacks are becoming more sophisticated, increasing the difficulty of defense.

risk_recommendations: Conduct regular and continuous cybersecurity audits.
Integrate cybersecurity considerations into all audit engagements.
Invest in advanced cyber defense technologies and staff training.
risks.trend: Cybersecurity risk remains elevated compared to 2019 levels and is among the top three highest risks consistently.
risks.likelihood: 78% of respondents rate cybersecurity as high or very high risk.
risks.impact: Potential for severe operational disruption, data breaches, financial loss, and reputational damage.
risks.risk_indicator: Frequency of cybersecurity audits conducted annually or continuously (approximately 70%).
contextual_variations: Cybersecurity risk is consistently high across all organization types including publicly traded, financial services, nonprofit, and public sector.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to IT systems not covered under cybersecurity, including system failures, outdated infrastructure, and integration challenges.

risk_driver.driver_description: Diverse and piecemeal IT systems increase complexity and risk of failure.
Technical and cost challenges associated with migrating to cloud platforms.

risk_recommendations: Conduct regular IT audits at least annually.
Invest in upgrading and integrating IT infrastructure.
Address supply chain challenges impacting IT investments.
risks.trend: IT risk remains a top risk with audit allocations increasing slightly since 2019.
risks.likelihood: 46% of respondents rate IT risk as high or very high risk.
risks.impact: Operational inefficiencies, increased costs, and potential service disruptions.
risks.risk_indicator: Frequency of IT audits conducted annually or continuously (approximately 70%).
contextual_variations: IT risk is rated slightly lower in publicly traded organizations compared to financial services.

risks.risk_description: Risks arising from reliance on third-party vendors and service providers, including IT service providers, which can introduce operational and compliance vulnerabilities.

risk_driver.driver_description: Heavy reliance on third parties for critical services increases exposure to external risks.
Third parties may not comply with regulatory requirements, impacting the organization.

risk_recommendations: Increase audit frequency of third-party relationships to align with risk levels.
Implement robust third-party risk management frameworks.
Regularly review and monitor third-party compliance and performance.
risks.trend: Third-party relationships is the third highest risk area but audit frequency lags behind risk level by 33 percentage points.
risks.likelihood: 44% of respondents rate third-party relationships as high or very high risk.
risks.impact: Operational disruptions, compliance breaches, and reputational damage.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency of third-party relationships (only 58% audit at least every 5 years).
contextual_variations: Third-party risk is rated higher in privately held organizations compared to other sectors.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to failure to comply with laws, regulations, and internal policies, excluding internal controls over financial reporting.

risk_driver.driver_description: Growing complexity and volume of regulations increase compliance challenges.

risk_recommendations: Conduct regular compliance audits.
Enhance regulatory monitoring and training programs.
Implement proactive compliance management systems.
risks.trend: Compliance risk remains significant with moderate to high risk ratings by 37% of respondents.
risks.likelihood: 37% rate this risk as high or very high.
risks.impact: Legal penalties, financial losses, and reputational harm.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for compliance/regulatory risk (9% continuous or annually, 15% every 2 to 5 years).
contextual_variations: Compliance risk is rated lower in publicly traded organizations compared to financial services.

risks.risk_description: Risks arising from failures in internal processes, people, and systems affecting day-to-day operations.

risk_driver.driver_description: Ineffective or outdated processes increase operational risk.
Errors, fraud, or lack of training among staff contribute to operational failures.

risk_recommendations: Increase focus on operational audits.
Implement process improvements and staff training.
Enhance risk management and monitoring systems.
risks.trend: Operational risk is consistently rated moderate to high by 61% of respondents.
risks.likelihood: 61% rate operational risk as moderate to high.
risks.impact: Disruptions to business activities, financial losses, and reduced service quality.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for operational risk (27% continuous or annually, 17% every 2 to 5 years).

risks.risk_name: Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) and Related Processes
risks.risk_description: Risks related to the effectiveness of enterprise risk management frameworks and processes.

risk_driver.driver_description: Inadequate risk identification, assessment, and mitigation processes.

risk_recommendations: Regularly audit ERM processes.
Strengthen risk governance and reporting.
Enhance risk culture and awareness across the organization.
risks.trend: ERM risk is rated moderate to high by 48% of respondents.
risks.likelihood: 48% rate ERM risk as moderate to high.
risks.impact: Increased exposure to unidentified or unmanaged risks.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for ERM and related processes (11% continuous or annually, 13% every 2 to 5 years).

risks.risk_description: Risks related to fraudulent activities within the organization, including financial fraud and ethical breaches.

risk_driver.driver_description: Gaps in controls increase vulnerability to fraud.
Weak ethical culture and whistleblower protections increase fraud risk.

risk_recommendations: Integrate fraud considerations into all audits.
Conduct dedicated fraud investigations and audits.
Strengthen ethics programs and whistleblower protections.
risks.trend: Fraud risk is a key focus with 73% rating it moderate or higher risk.
risks.likelihood: 73% rate fraud risk as moderate or higher.
risks.impact: Financial losses, legal consequences, and reputational damage.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for fraud risk (24% continuous or annually, 17% every 2 to 5 years).

risks.risk_description: Risks arising from ineffective governance structures and poor organizational culture impacting decision-making and compliance.

risk_driver.driver_description: Lack of oversight and accountability.
Poor ethical standards and low employee engagement.

risk_recommendations: Conduct governance and culture audits.
Enhance board and management oversight.
Promote ethical culture and employee engagement.
risks.trend: Governance and culture risk is rated moderate or higher by 68% of respondents.
risks.likelihood: 68% rate governance and culture risk as moderate or higher.
risks.impact: Poor decision-making, compliance failures, and reputational harm.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for governance and culture (20% continuous or annually, 24% every 2 to 5 years).

risks.risk_description: Risks related to inaccuracies or failures in financial reporting and internal controls over financial reporting.

risk_driver.driver_description: Increasing complexity of financial reporting standards.
Weaknesses in controls over financial reporting processes.

risk_recommendations: Conduct frequent audits of financial reporting and ICFR.
Implement strong internal controls and compliance programs.
Ensure Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance where applicable.
risks.trend: Financial reporting risk remains significant, especially in publicly traded organizations with SOX requirements.
risks.likelihood: 40% rate financial reporting risk as high or very high.
risks.impact: Financial misstatements, regulatory penalties, and loss of investor confidence.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for financial reporting (including ICFR) (15% continuous or annually, 24% every 2 to 5 years).
contextual_variations: Higher audit allocation in publicly traded and SOX-implemented organizations.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to the need for cost control and expense reduction impacting operational efficiency and financial health.

risk_driver.driver_description: Market and economic conditions driving the need for cost reductions.

risk_recommendations: Increase audit focus on cost and expense reduction initiatives.
Implement robust financial monitoring and control mechanisms.
risks.trend: Cost/expense reduction risk is trending up since 2020 and is notably higher in nonprofit organizations.
risks.likelihood: 48% rate cost/expense reduction risk as moderate or higher.
risks.impact: Financial strain, reduced service quality, and operational challenges.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for cost/expense reduction (6% continuous or annually, 31% every 2 to 5 years).
contextual_variations: Higher risk level in nonprofit organizations.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to sustainability practices and non-financial reporting, including environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors.

risk_driver.driver_description: Growing demand for transparency and sustainability reporting.

risk_recommendations: Integrate sustainability considerations into audit plans.
Enhance reporting and compliance with ESG standards.
risks.trend: Sustainability risk is increasing, with more than 60% of public sector respondents rating it moderate to very high risk.
risks.likelihood: 24% rate sustainability risk as high or very high.
risks.impact: Reputational damage, regulatory penalties, and loss of stakeholder trust.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for sustainability/non-financial reporting (3% continuous or annually, 8% every 2 to 5 years).
contextual_variations: More prominent in public sector organizations.

risks.risk_description: Risks related to the adequacy of support provided to external auditors, impacting audit quality and compliance.

risk_driver.driver_description: Limited resources and coordination challenges with external auditors.

risk_recommendations: Enhance collaboration and support for external audit processes.
Allocate sufficient resources to facilitate external audits.
risks.trend: Support for external audit is audited more frequently than its risk level would suggest, with a 45 percentage point higher audit frequency than risk.
risks.likelihood: 47% rate this risk as moderate or higher.
risks.impact: Potential for audit delays, increased costs, and compliance issues.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for support for external audit (24% continuous or annually, 26% every 2 to 5 years).

risks.risk_description: Risks related to ineffective governance and poor organizational culture impacting overall risk management and compliance.

risk_driver.driver_description: Insufficient board and management oversight.
Weak ethical culture and employee engagement.

risk_recommendations: Conduct governance and culture audits regularly.
Promote ethical behavior and accountability.
risks.trend: Governance and culture risk is rated moderate or higher by 68% of respondents.
risks.likelihood: 68% rate this risk as moderate or higher.
risks.impact: Poor decision-making, compliance failures, and reputational damage.
risks.risk_indicator: Audit frequency for governance and culture (20% continuous or annually, 24% every 2 to 5 years).
